summary:
SpaceXplorer – Beyond the Galaxy is an interactive, browser-based space exploration learning game developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It allows players to explore 10 space destinations, complete science-based missions, answer quiz questions, and manage resources such as fuel, energy, and oxygen. The game also includes a scoring system, a discovery log, and an educational section explaining NASA Mission Architecture through four mission segments: Launch, Space, Ground, and User.

SpaceXplorer addresses the challenge by making space exploration concepts more engaging and accessible through interactive gameplay rather than only theoretical learning. It encourages players to explore destinations, solve science questions, and understand how space missions are organized.

This project is important because it promotes curiosity about space, improves scientific awareness, and makes learning enjoyable, especially for students and beginners.
details: Project Details: SpaceXplorer – Beyond the Galaxy 1. What does the project do and how does it work? SpaceXplorer is an interactive, browser-based educational space exploration game. It allows players to explore 10 space destinations, including Earth, Mars, Saturn, the Moon, Neptune, Europa, and other locations. Players select destinations, complete missions, and answer five randomly selected science questions from a bank of 30 questions. During missions, they manage three resources: fuel, energy, and oxygen. Successful mission completion earns points, unlocks new destinations, and adds discoveries to the Discovery Log. The project also includes an educational NASA Mission Architecture section that explains four major mission segments: Launch, Space, Ground, and User. It introduces a simplified six-stage mission design process. 2. What are the benefits? - Makes space science more interactive and enjoyable. - Helps beginners learn basic space concepts. - Encourages curiosity, exploration, and problem-solving. - Introduces the basic organization of space science missions. - Combines educational content with game-based learning. 3. What is the intended impact? The main aim is to encourage students and beginners to become more interested in space science. By combining exploration, quizzes, resource management, and mission progression, SpaceXplorer makes learning more engaging and accessible. 4. What tools and technologies were used? - HTML: To create the structure of the website. - CSS: To design the interface, layout, and visual appearance. - JavaScript: To implement game logic, missions, quizzes, scoring, resource management, and destination unlocking. - Visual Studio Code: For writing and editing the code. - Web Browser: For running and testing the game. The project is a software-based prototype and does not require additional hardware. 5. How is the project creative? SpaceXplorer combines space exploration with educational gaming. Instead of simply presenting information about planets and space missions, it allows players to explore destinations, complete challenges, manage resources, and unlock new locations. The addition of NASA Mission Architecture concepts connects gameplay with real-world space mission organization. 6. What factors did we consider? During development, we considered: - Beginner-friendly gameplay and simple navigation. - Educational value and scientific awareness. - Mission progression and player engagement. - Resource management to make missions more challenging. - Clear presentation of space mission concepts. - Accessibility through a standard web browser. Conclusion SpaceXplorer demonstrates how simple web technologies can create an engaging educational experience. It aims to inspire curiosity about the universe and make space science easier and more enjoyable to explore.
